Last Thursday, September 24th, I went to the Montijo store where I usually shop and ordered concentrated floor disinfectant, three 1-liter bottles. I had never placed an online order before. I have three dogs, and they always go to the store to buy what I need. I only placed this order because I saw the product in the window display, and the saleswoman who helped me said that someone had cancelled their order, and because of this cancellation, the product was in the backlog. Well, two days later, on Saturday, the product arrived at the store. I received the email and the text message. When I went there, I found the small cardboard box open, and instead of the three products, there were only 12. I started questioning that this was incorrect, that this was illegal, that I should have been informed, and that it could only be opened in my presence. Even worse, not all the products were there, which clearly demonstrates a huge suspicion that someone had diverted the product, especially since the manager, Dina, insisted on a refund, which I didn't want. Then the manager said that this is a standard procedure for the stores and that... Well, I called two stores I go to in Lisbon, and I called the Arquivo store in Setúbal. It's not standard procedure unless the boxes are very bulky with small deliveries; they don't have space to leave them, so they might open them. But under no circumstances should my order have been opened, and it's very likely they diverted the product. I had to wait another 3 days, and now I don't have time to go there to pick it up. I want to emphasize that this manager acted in bad faith twice: by refusing to refund the money and not asking me if I wanted the product or a refund, and then by using the name of the company and saying it's standard procedure for all Arquivo stores, violating Portuguese law and opening customer packages without their presence!!!
I loved it, and I found everything I needed, not to mention the excellent service.
I had to go to a much smaller store in the same chain because they didn't have the food I usually buy.

My experience with Kiwoko raises serious questions about the quality of the products they sell and how they handle situations related to animal safety.
I purchased the "Tootoy! Chew Dental Hygiene Cactus" toy, intended for canine chewing, and it presented a structural failure in less than 5 minutes of normal use. The product was quickly damaged, allowing the animal to release and ingest fragments of rubber.
It is important to emphasize that this type of occurrence does not fall under a scenario of progressive wear, but rather a clear inadequacy of the product for its purpose. A toy designed for chewing must guarantee a minimum level of resistance compatible with predictable use. The rapid degradation observed compromises not only durability but, above all, safety.

The ingestion of materials such as rubber is a known risk, and can lead to gastrointestinal complications, including obstructions, which makes this type of failure particularly relevant from the point of view of product safety.
After contacting customer support, the response received was based solely on transferring responsibility to the consumer, invoking the need for supervision. However, this indication does not replace or reduce the obligation to ensure that the product is safe under normal conditions of use. Supervision is a complementary measure, not a mechanism to mitigate immediate performance failures.

The approach adopted demonstrates a lack of substantial analysis of the problem presented, as well as an underestimation of the potential risk associated with the product.

In short, this is a product that does not show minimum characteristics of suitability for its function and a response from the company that does not reflect an effective concern for animal safety or the quality of the goods provided.

“After further contact, the response remained unchanged and the case was closed without a concrete analysis of the safety issue raised.”

I do not recommend it.

We started going to this store more often after getting our pets, but I won't be going back because my 6-year-old son experienced an act of xenophobia... perpetrated by an employee on March 24th, 2026, around 4 PM. This person, so full of antipathy, treating a child badly says more about her bad character than anything else! From the moment an employee considers themselves superior to the customer, that person is not prepared to deal with people! The store is complete; I was about to pay for the pet carrier, but after the incident, I abandoned the carrier there and left! Besides, how could I leave my money in a place where good service is essential and crucial! To the young man who served me on previous occasions, I offer my congratulations for always treating us very well and with a high level of professionalism! As a business owner, I would give this "employee" a warning because the store depends on customers to stay afloat!
